sentence: This project redesigns human inner ear cells grown in a culture dish so they work better for testing drug or gene therapies.
This project studies how virus vectors behave in the kidney and evolves vectors aimed at the kidney to deliver gene therapy.
This project provides tested stocks of wild-type and mutant viruses and lentiviral libraries that the research groups of the program need.
This project tests combined treatments for alcohol use disorder and alcohol-associated liver disease in patients with advanced liver disease.
This project builds microfluidic system components to help study how biomolecules change with illness, disease and disease treatments.
This project develops a deep learning method to predict risk of orofacial clefts and test gene associations in large genetic data.
This project tests whether stimulating the vagus nerve through the ear can help repair myelin and restore function after demyelinating injury.
This project studies three treatments that act on circuits for an intractable disorder, using imaging to see how they affect treatment response.
This project provides an acoustic liquid handler that helps researchers screen many potential treatments for cancer, infections and other diseases faster.
This project builds software that uses magnetic resonance imaging scans and deep learning to measure how neurofluid moves and clears in neurodegeneration.
This project builds deep learning tools that turn inhale and exhale CT image pairs into functional information to measure how severe the disease is.
This project builds a sequencing method that finds the RNA targets of snoRNA and maps them across many types of cancer cells.
This project tests whether magnetic resonance imaging can detect inflammation in blood vessels of the head and eyes in giant cell arteritis.
This project supports research that connects genetics and neuroscience discoveries to ways of preventing and treating psychiatric disorders.
This project follows patients with coronary disease who had bypass surgery or stenting, to compare outcomes including death and quality of life.
This project offers training in human genetics using a biobank of many subjects for studies of human genetic variation.
This project studies whether aging measures from blood DNA methylation can explain heart disease risk in breast cancer survivors.
This project studies what triggers macrophages to interact with stem and progenitor cells and what those interactions do during development and regeneration.
This project uses machine learning on long-term national data to find what drives alcohol risk among sexual and gender minority groups.
This project studies which molecular pathways drive early type 1 diabetes by using spatial proteomics and lipidomics on human islet tissue from patients.
